## From College Struggles to App Success: The Story Behind Twos

Parker Klein first conceptualized Twos in 2015 during his time at Vanderbilt University. Struggling with depression, he began documenting his thoughts in a Google Doc. While writing provided relief, the disjointed nature of traditional note-taking tools led to frustration and limited engagement. [...] ## What on Earth Are Twos PALs and Why Should You Care?

Twos PALs, short for Personal Active Lists, are AI-powered tools built into the platform that analyze what users write and generate meaningful, time-saving outcomes. Unlike generic AI integrations that flood the interface with automated content, PALs operate with purpose and precision.

The feature works behind the scenes to scan input, identify intent, and act only when relevant. This includes recognizing task-oriented text, dates, and content categories. PALs can set reminders, create events, retrieve product links, and suggest actions based on what’s written. If no match is found, no suggestion is made, maintaining a clean interface. [...] Twos PALs is an AI-powered feature that analyzes what users write and provides contextual actions like reminders, event creation, and product links without cluttering the interface. Built by Parker Klein and Joe Steilberg, Twos emphasizes simplicity, speed, and privacy. The app supports seamless organization while allowing users full control over their information.

## The problem

Today, we need so many tools and sources to keep track of life and what we need to do.

We use lists, calendars, browser tabs, text yourself, post-it notes, task managers… the list goes on and on.

And most of these tools don’t sync or consolidate our information.

They are static and don’t help us get things done.

Making a list is another manual task and sharing the list can be a challenge.

Most of our information ends up lost or thrown away so we don’t have a dependable record or memory. [...] AI chatbots and assistants are said to be helpful, but there isn’t a path to how we get there. They can interrupt our flow and big companies are selling and training off of your personal data.

There is no good way to write things down, manage your life, control your information, and get things done automatically.
